newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-NZ'S FIJI WIN COMES AT BIG PRICE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ'S FIJI WIN COMES AT BIG PRICE.

text.p: The All Blacks' legendary flanker Michael Jones underwent surgery on Sunday after suffering a severe knee injury during Saturday's rugby union test against Fiji, which New Zealand won 71-5.
The injury meant Jones, a veteran of 51 tests, was unlikely to play again this season and the match against lowly ranked Fiji may have been the last of his 10-year career.
Jones, 32, is no stranger to injury -- having damaged the same knee against Argentina in 1989.
Doctors doubted he would ever walk properly again after that encounter but Jones, a devout Christian who refuses to play on Sundays, recovered and regained his All Black jersey.
"Michael Jones has done so many amazing things coming back from injuries. Don't write him off," Hart said after Saturday's match.
Another worry for the All Black selectors was fly-half Andrew Mehrtens, who was also put in doubt with a hamstring injury.
The injuries mean selectors will make two changes to their team to play Argentina in the first of two rugby tests in Wellington on Saturday.
Otago's Taine Randell will move to the blindside flanker while Auckland's Carlos Spencer make his test debut at Athletic Park in place of Mehrtens.
Hart said Randell would do as good a job at No. 6 as he did on Saturday in the No. 8 jersey in place of Zinzan Brooke.
"No one is going to fill Michael Jones' shoes. It is an impossibility, he is a player apart in the game," Hart said.
"But Taine is someone this panel has a lot of faith in and I think it was vindicated last night," Hart said.
